# `synap` command reference

Synap CLI — connect AI agents to your data pod

228 commands. Hidden commands and hidden options are omitted here (5 hidden commands); `cli.json` lists them with `"hidden": true`.

Every command also accepts `-h, --help`.

## Commands

- [`synap init`](#synap-init) — Full setup: connect to a Synap pod and install the skill
- [`synap launch`](#synap-launch) — Stand up a NEW company/OS on a pod — creates a project + its core workspaces (interactive)
- [`synap connect`](#synap-connect) — Plug something into your pod: an AI agent (claude-code, cursor, codex, …) or a tool/account (gmail, github, …)
- [`synap pods`](#synap-pods) — Manage multiple Synap pod profiles and switch between them
  - [`synap pods list`](#synap-pods-list) — List all configured pod profiles
  - [`synap pods add`](#synap-pods-add) — Connect a new pod and save as a named profile
  - [`synap pods use`](#synap-pods-use) — Switch active pod and propagate credentials to all agent surfaces
  - [`synap pods update`](#synap-pods-update) — Change a saved pod's URL in place (verifies health + whether the key must be recreated)
  - [`synap pods remove`](#synap-pods-remove) — Remove a pod profile
  - [`synap pods reconnect`](#synap-pods-reconnect) — Re-authenticate a saved pod (refresh API key without re-entering the URL)
- [`synap status`](#synap-status) — Show Synap pod health and API status
- [`synap doctor`](#synap-doctor) — Coherence preflight: pod host resolves, key authenticates, workspace/project exist on THIS pod, and why each configured key does or does not work — catches config drift in one call
- [`synap versions`](#synap-versions) — Show LOCAL vs NPM vs CONTROL-PLANE vs POD version drift for workspace-templates, api-types, and capabilities
- [`synap whoami`](#synap-whoami) — Show key owner vs EFFECTIVE user (+ isAgent), scopes/workspace, and flag env-vs-surface key divergence
- [`synap update`](#synap-update) — Show how to update the CLI
- [`synap switch`](#synap-switch) — Switch active pod (interactive picker if no name given)
- [`synap connections`](#synap-connections) — Show everything connected: which pod each agent points at, and which tools the pod has connected
- [`synap app`](#synap-app) — Connect an app in this repo to your pod (synap.app.json)
  - [`synap app init`](#synap-app-init) — Write synap.app.json (asks name, pod, permissions) and register the app
  - [`synap app connect`](#synap-app-connect) — Request the app's access, await approval, then write its key into the deploy target
- [`synap mcp`](#synap-mcp) — Connect any AI client to your pod's MCP server (the ambient tool layer)
  - [`synap mcp url`](#synap-mcp-url) — Print a ready-to-paste MCP connection (URL + key + snippets) for UI clients like ChatGPT
  - [`synap mcp verify`](#synap-mcp-verify) — Health-check: is the pod's /mcp endpoint reachable and the key valid?
  - [`synap mcp bridge`](#synap-mcp-bridge) — Stdio MCP server for Claude Code: forwards to the pod and names the conversation (spawned by Claude Code, not run by hand)
  - [`synap mcp use-bridge`](#synap-mcp-use-bridge) — Connect Claude Code through the stdio bridge, so work can be traced to and reopened in its conversation
  - [`synap mcp connect`](#synap-mcp-connect) — Write the MCP config for a file-configurable client (Claude Code, Cursor, Desktop, ChatGPT, …) — alias of `synap agents add <client>`
  - [`synap mcp connect-chatgpt`](#synap-mcp-connect-chatgpt) — Connect ChatGPT (web) to Synap — API-key connector to your pod
  - [`synap mcp connect-chatgpt-oauth`](#synap-mcp-connect-chatgpt-oauth) — Connect ChatGPT (web) via Control Plane OAuth — multi-pod, no key to paste
  - [`synap mcp connect-claude`](#synap-mcp-connect-claude) — Print the claude.ai (web) OAuth connection steps — paste a URL, approve in the browser, done
  - [`synap mcp ui-setup`](#synap-mcp-ui-setup) — Print the exact form fields to fill in the client's MCP/Connector UI (ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, etc.)
- [`synap login`](#synap-login) — Connect your Synap account (private templates) + your pods
- [`synap orient`](#synap-orient) — Show a lightweight lens map: who you are, your projects (companies/initiatives), and workspaces (operational domains)
- [`synap digest`](#synap-digest) — Summarize what's in a workspace or project (counts + key entities)
- [`synap diagnose`](#synap-diagnose) — See what an AI did — the run feed, or one run's nodes (by id or flow name)
- [`synap use`](#synap-use) — Set the active workspace (by ID or name) — short form of `synap workspace use`. Default scope: this directory
- [`synap project`](#synap-project) — Manage + focus the project lens (a commitment, spanning workspaces): list, new, use, clear
  - [`synap project list`](#synap-project-list) — List projects on the active pod, with the pinned one marked (bare `synap project` runs this)
  - [`synap project new`](#synap-project-new) — Create a project (a commitment you are driving, with whom) on the active pod, then guide you to pin + add to it
  - [`synap project use`](#synap-project-use) — Pin the active project (durable, like `synap use <workspace>`). Ref = uuid, slug, or <pod>/<slug> — cross-pod refs switch the active pod too
  - [`synap project clear`](#synap-project-clear) — Clear the active project focus (durable by default)
  - [`synap project purge`](#synap-project-purge) — HARD teardown: delete a project + its pod-wide-exclusive entities (owner-only, irreversible)
- [`synap lens`](#synap-lens) — Show the effective lens (workspace + project + focus session) and WHICH rung set each one
- [`synap ask`](#synap-ask) — Ask your pod anything — returns a synthesized answer with its sources
- [`synap capture`](#synap-capture) — Capture knowledge: smart `capture "<free text>"` (AI structures it). For canonical typed Knowledge, use `create entity --profile=knowledge --props='{"knowledgeForm":"insight\|caution"}'`.
- [`synap import`](#synap-import) — Import files, folders, or URLs into the pod (AI capture pipeline, or Superwhisper store-first)
- [`synap upload`](#synap-upload) — Upload a file to the pod as an entity (>10MB goes direct to storage: video ≤500MB, audio ≤100MB, zip ≤200MB)
- [`synap subscribe`](#synap-subscribe) — Stream pod events as NDJSON (long-poll)
- [`synap home`](#synap-home) — Show the active workspace's home bento layout (what cells are on screen)
- [`synap context`](#synap-context) — Session-start context: knowledge, proposals, tasks, active sessions
- [`synap discover`](#synap-discover) — Runtime discovery: entity profiles with property schemas + CLI command tree
- [`synap workspace`](#synap-workspace) — Manage + focus the workspace lens (an operational domain): list, use, clear
  - [`synap workspace use`](#synap-workspace-use) — Pin the active workspace by ID or name (durable, like `synap use <workspace>`). Default scope: this directory
  - [`synap workspace list`](#synap-workspace-list) — List workspaces you belong to (bare `synap workspace` runs this)
  - [`synap workspace clear`](#synap-workspace-clear) — Clear the active workspace focus (durable by default)
  - [`synap workspace provision-agent`](#synap-workspace-provision-agent) — Provision an agent-owned workspace and set it as active (idempotent)
  - [`synap workspace purge`](#synap-workspace-purge) — HARD teardown: delete a workspace + all its entities and blobs (owner-only, irreversible)
  - [`synap workspace archive`](#synap-workspace-archive) — Archive a workspace (hides it, pauses its workspace automations). Governed: agents propose
  - [`synap workspace restore`](#synap-workspace-restore) — Restore an archived workspace (by id). Re-enables nothing; lists automations still paused
  - [`synap workspace rename`](#synap-workspace-rename) — Rename a workspace. Governed: agents propose
- [`synap entity`](#synap-entity) — Entity operations: move
  - [`synap entity move`](#synap-entity-move) — Move entities into another workspace. Governed per entity: moved / proposed / errors
- [`synap list`](#synap-list) — List pod resources
  - [`synap list workspaces`](#synap-list-workspaces) — List workspaces you belong to
  - [`synap list profiles`](#synap-list-profiles) — List entity profile types available in a workspace
  - [`synap list views`](#synap-list-views) — List views in a workspace (whiteboard, kanban, bento, …)
  - [`synap list entities`](#synap-list-entities) — List entities on the pod
- [`synap show`](#synap-show) — Show an entity with its properties and all linked relations
- [`synap facet`](#synap-facet) — Manage roles attached to an entity (client, partner, contact, …)
  - [`synap facet attach`](#synap-facet-attach) — Attach a role to an entity
  - [`synap facet list`](#synap-facet-list) — List the roles attached to an entity
  - [`synap facet detach`](#synap-facet-detach) — Detach a role — pass the facet id, or --entity <id> --role <slug>
- [`synap proposals`](#synap-proposals) — Review and act on governance proposals
  - [`synap proposals list`](#synap-proposals-list) — List governance proposals (default: the pending queue)
  - [`synap proposals approve`](#synap-proposals-approve) — Approve a pending proposal (interactive only — requires a TTY and a typed confirmation)
  - [`synap proposals reject`](#synap-proposals-reject) — Reject a pending proposal
  - [`synap proposals await`](#synap-proposals-await) — Block until a proposal is decided. Exit 0 approved · 1 rejected/expired/withdrawn · 2 timeout
- [`synap worker`](#synap-worker) — Run Claude Code unattended here for the sessions handed to an agent
- [`synap session`](#synap-session) — Manage focus sessions (goal-bound AI work rooms)
  - [`synap session start`](#synap-session-start) — Start a new focus session and return its ID
  - [`synap session list`](#synap-session-list) — List focus sessions in the active workspace
  - [`synap session get`](#synap-session-get) — Show details for a specific focus session (works for project-scoped sessions)
  - [`synap session update`](#synap-session-update) — Update a focus session's progress, status, stage or goal
  - [`synap session close`](#synap-session-close) — End a focus session (proposal pack) and optionally attach a recap
  - [`synap session attach`](#synap-session-attach) — Attach a session to this terminal — all hub calls tag X-Session-Id until detached
  - [`synap session detach`](#synap-session-detach) — Remove the active session from this terminal
  - [`synap session current`](#synap-session-current) — Show the active session for this terminal (SYNAP_SESSION_ID, Claude-session lens, or .synap/lens.json)
  - [`synap session evidence`](#synap-session-evidence) — Post your own pass/fail report for one evidence-checked acceptance criterion
  - [`synap session evaluate`](#synap-session-evaluate) — Run every pending acceptance-criterion check (evidence, capability, judge) and print the verdicts
  - [`synap session wait`](#synap-session-wait) — Block until the human replies in the session room (or, with --events, until the session changes), then print it. Session: the argument, else the one attached to this terminal. Exit 0 replied · 1 timeout · 2 failure (auth/network/broken read); with --hook: 2 wake · 0 anything else
  - [`synap session post`](#synap-session-post) — Message ANOTHER of your sessions' agent: blocked_on_you / handoff may wake it, done / fyi never do. Replying to a message that woke you? Pass its id as --cause. Exit 0 delivered · 1 pod does not deliver agent messages · 2 failure
- [`synap hooks`](#synap-hooks) — Claude Code hooks that connect a terminal to its Synap session
  - [`synap hooks install-wake`](#synap-hooks-install-wake) — Add the wake hook (a Stop hook running `synap session wait --hook`) to this project's .claude/settings.json — idempotent, other hooks kept
- [`synap playbook`](#synap-playbook) — Run playbooks — governed, reusable processes
  - [`synap playbook run`](#synap-playbook-run) — Run a playbook by name or id, optionally on a subject entity
- [`synap track`](#synap-track) — Manage tracks — the goals a project pursues
  - [`synap track list`](#synap-track-list) — List a project's goals (the active project lens); with no project in scope, every goal on the pod
  - [`synap track show`](#synap-track-show) — Show one track: its steps and where it stands
  - [`synap track start`](#synap-track-start) — Start a track — a goal — on a project
  - [`synap track update`](#synap-track-update) — Set a goal's direction, KPI and what it holds (each field is written whole; kpi is merged)
  - [`synap track accept`](#synap-track-accept) — The goal's judge decides a claimed criterion: accepted \| changes_asked \| rejected (a person's act)
  - [`synap track advance`](#synap-track-advance) — Legacy (tracks with steps): move a track to a step; prints the session that step offers
  - [`synap track status`](#synap-track-status) — Move a track: proposed\|agreed\|ready\|active\|paused\|completed (Closed)\|archived (Dropped). Closing needs --verdict met\|partly_met\|not_met (an operation closes retired, and only one does); dropping should carry no_longer_needed\|impossible\|replaced\|mistake (impossible and replaced need --verdict-reason). Both are final — reopen makes a new version.
  - [`synap track reopen`](#synap-track-reopen) — Reopen a closed or dropped goal as a NEW version (the old one keeps its verdict)
  - [`synap track params`](#synap-track-params) — Answer the method's params as key=value (merged; key=null clears one)
  - [`synap track start-step`](#synap-track-start-step) — Legacy (tracks with steps): start one step's session — on a track with no steps, use 'session start --track'
- [`synap goal`](#synap-goal) — Goals — what people call a track
  - [`synap goal convert`](#synap-goal-convert) — Make a goal, objective or OKR entity a goal (once; the entity is kept and linked)
- [`synap skill`](#synap-skill) — Execute a skill in an autonomous workspace session
  - [`synap skill gather-context`](#synap-skill-gather-context) — Gather pod KG + local context (CLAUDE.md, .claude/kg-verify) for a session
  - [`synap skill suggest`](#synap-skill-suggest) — Search the skill knowledge base by topic or keyword
  - [`synap skill get`](#synap-skill-get) — Fetch a skill from the knowledge base by slug and print its body
  - [`synap skill add`](#synap-skill-add) — Add skill(s) to your pod from: bundled · a local path · ~/.claude/skills/ · owner/repo · a git URL
  - [`synap skill list`](#synap-skill-list) — List the instruction skills installed on your pod
  - [`synap skill approve`](#synap-skill-approve) — Approve a skill so it loads (agent-authored skills are born unapproved)
  - [`synap skill remove`](#synap-skill-remove) — Remove a skill from your pod by slug
  - [`synap skill sync`](#synap-skill-sync) — Bulk-import local skills from ~/.claude/skills/ into the pod
  - [`synap skill verify-code`](#synap-skill-verify-code) — Run the project's type-check/test gate and store the result on the session
- [`synap browse`](#synap-browse) — Browse entities in the active workspace, optionally filtered by profile type or role
- [`synap observe`](#synap-observe) — Write and recall pod-wide user observations (AI-maintained user model)
  - [`synap observe write`](#synap-observe-write) — Record an observation about the user (pod-scoped, AI-maintained)
  - [`synap observe recall`](#synap-observe-recall) — Search recorded user observations
- [`synap get`](#synap-get) — Get a single pod resource
  - [`synap get entity`](#synap-get-entity) — Get an entity by ID
- [`synap create`](#synap-create) — Create pod resources
  - [`synap create entity`](#synap-create-entity) — Create a new entity
  - [`synap create relation`](#synap-create-relation) — Create a typed relation between two entities
- [`synap set`](#synap-set) — Update pod resources
  - [`synap set entity`](#synap-set-entity) — Update entity properties
- [`synap agents`](#synap-agents) — Manage agent principals on your pod (one per type for you; local keys are a cache)
  - [`synap agents list`](#synap-agents-list) — List your agents on this pod (one per type). Use --local for ~/.synap cache only.
  - [`synap agents add`](#synap-agents-add) — Bring an agent into the pod: a client (claude-code, cursor, codex, …), your own (--name → URL + key), or pick from this machine (no kind)
  - [`synap agents create`](#synap-agents-create) — Deprecated — use `synap agents add` (same flags)
  - [`synap agents rotate-key`](#synap-agents-rotate-key) — Rotate the Hub Protocol API key for an agent (local cache only)
  - [`synap agents remove`](#synap-agents-remove) — Remove a named agent identity (local cache only)
  - [`synap agents info`](#synap-agents-info) — Show details for a named agent identity (local cache only)
- [`synap agent`](#synap-agent) — Run autonomous agent loops against the IS, or schedule recurring goals
  - [`synap agent ask`](#synap-agent-ask) — Send one message to the workspace's deployed agent and print its reply (multi-turn: reuses one thread)
  - [`synap agent chat`](#synap-agent-chat) — Interactive REPL conversation with the workspace's deployed agent
  - [`synap agent run`](#synap-agent-run) — Run an autonomous agent toward a goal using the Intelligence Service
  - [`synap agent schedule`](#synap-agent-schedule) — Add, list, or remove recurring agent schedules
  - [`synap agent tick`](#synap-agent-tick) — Check due schedules and run them — wire this to crontab: `0 * * * * synap agent tick`
- [`synap automate`](#synap-automate) — Ask the workspace agent to prepare a governed automation proposal
- [`synap rule`](#synap-rule) — State a standing rule in plain language — classified, shown, then governed-created
  - [`synap rule list`](#synap-rule-list) — List rules with their intent, scope, and whether a behaviour is attached
- [`synap automation`](#synap-automation) — Create, manage, and inspect pod automations
  - [`synap automation list`](#synap-automation-list) — List automations on the pod
  - [`synap automation describe`](#synap-automation-describe) — Show full details of an automation
  - [`synap automation create`](#synap-automation-create) — Create an automation (quick flags or --from file.yaml)
  - [`synap automation enable`](#synap-automation-enable) — Activate an automation
  - [`synap automation disable`](#synap-automation-disable) — Pause an automation
  - [`synap automation delete`](#synap-automation-delete) — Delete an automation
  - [`synap automation schema`](#synap-automation-schema) — Fetch the automation DSL schema from the pod (AI context)
- [`synap graph`](#synap-graph) — Low-level BFS graph traversal from an entity (prefer `synap ask` — graph is one of its signals)
- [`synap centrality`](#synap-centrality) — Inspect PageRank centrality (entity_centrality) and trigger a recompute
  - [`synap centrality status`](#synap-centrality-status) — Show whether PageRank centrality has populated + the top central entities
  - [`synap centrality recompute`](#synap-centrality-recompute) — Enqueue a PageRank centrality recompute (runs in the background)
- [`synap events`](#synap-events) — Show event chain for an entity or recent pod events
- [`synap view`](#synap-view) — Manage views
  - [`synap view create`](#synap-view-create) — Create a view (table, kanban, bento, …)
  - [`synap view list`](#synap-view-list) — List views in the active workspace
  - [`synap view arrange`](#synap-view-arrange) — Replace the widget arrangement of a bento view
- [`synap explain`](#synap-explain) — Full capability map — what Synap can do and how (no network required)
- [`synap open`](#synap-open) — Open in the Synap desktop app. Use: open <kind> <id> or open <id> (auto-resolves type)
- [`synap doc`](#synap-doc) — Create and update markdown documents on the pod
  - [`synap doc create`](#synap-doc-create) — Create a new markdown document
  - [`synap doc update`](#synap-doc-update) — Update a document's content: the whole body, or one section (--section). Governed: an agent's edit is proposed.
  - [`synap doc reference`](#synap-doc-reference) — Create an external reference document (points at a URL — no bytes stored)
- [`synap cell`](#synap-cell) — Define and bundle frame cells for the Synap runtime
  - [`synap cell define`](#synap-cell-define) — Create or update a frame cell on the pod from ESM source
  - [`synap cell build`](#synap-cell-build) — Bundle a multi-file cell/app into a single ESM module the runtime expects
- [`synap artifact`](#synap-artifact) — Create HTML artifacts as Synap cells: an HTML/JS page that opens in the desktop app and can read pod data
  - [`synap artifact create`](#synap-artifact-create) — Define a cell from a local HTML file (governed: an agent key files a proposal)
- [`synap connect-service`](#synap-connect-service) — Connect an external service (Google, GitHub, Notion, Linear, Slack, …)
- [`synap tools`](#synap-tools) — Add and manage external service tools and their credentials
  - [`synap tools list`](#synap-tools-list) — List available tools and their connection status
  - [`synap tools connect`](#synap-tools-connect) — Connect a credential to a tool (OAuth via the connection broker, or vault)
  - [`synap tools sync`](#synap-tools-sync) — Trigger a manual sync for a connected tool
  - [`synap tools disconnect`](#synap-tools-disconnect) — Revoke a tool's connection
  - [`synap tools schema`](#synap-tools-schema) — Fetch tool schema and supported providers (AI context)
- [`synap pod`](#synap-pod) — Show the whole configured pod — workspaces (with provenance), capabilities/automations/playbooks, and feed links
  - [`synap pod adopt`](#synap-pod-adopt) — Link an orphan/ad-hoc workspace (by name or id) to a matching template — makes it version-tracked
- [`synap vendor`](#synap-vendor) — Your marketplace publisher profile (what packages are attributed to)
  - [`synap vendor create`](#synap-vendor-create) — Create your publisher profile — do this BEFORE your first publish
  - [`synap vendor show`](#synap-vendor-show) — Show whether you have a publisher profile
- [`synap market`](#synap-market) — Browse + install packages (workspaces, capabilities, skills, workflows, views, cells) into a project
  - [`synap market install`](#synap-market-install) — Install a package by slug into a project — workspaces install now; other types route you to the right surface
  - [`synap market update`](#synap-market-update) — Check installed packages for drift against the catalog, and re-apply the ones that are stale (all with --yes, specific ones with explicit slugs)
  - [`synap market installed`](#synap-market-installed) — List packages installed on this pod — a pure read, no writes (pairs with 'market update' to check drift)
  - [`synap market workspaces`](#synap-market-workspaces) — List your workspaces with their template-attachment status — find the one that isn't attached yet (pure read)
  - [`synap market attach`](#synap-market-attach) — Reconcile a marketplace template onto an existing workspace + version-stamp it — how you relink a workspace installed before the marketplace
  - [`synap market scaffold`](#synap-market-scaffold) — Write a minimal valid <slug>.template.yaml to edit in place (refuses to overwrite)
  - [`synap market validate`](#synap-market-validate) — Validate a local template file against the shared template validator — fast author feedback
  - [`synap market publish`](#synap-market-publish) — Validate then publish a template (or a standalone cell/view package) to the marketplace (private by default) — pass a file, --from-workspace <id>, or --from-project <id>. Non-official publish never uses the synap-official vendor. Founder: --official [slug...] publishes the official catalog from the monorepo checkout (alias of `synap catalog publish --official --kind workspace`)
  - [`synap market unpublish`](#synap-market-unpublish) — Flip a published package back to private (owner only)
- [`synap templates`](#synap-templates) — See every workspace's template status (attached, drifted, or unattached) and connect them — the one home for template health
  - [`synap templates attach`](#synap-templates-attach) — Connect a workspace (by NAME or id) to a template — suggests the right one so you don't guess a slug
  - [`synap templates update`](#synap-templates-update) — Apply template updates — 'update all' (or --yes) for every drifted workspace, or name specific slugs. Bare 'update' previews what's available.
  - [`synap templates retire`](#synap-templates-retire) — Move a retired template's space into its replacement (by template slug, workspace name or id). Shows the plan, asks, then moves through the pod — never deletes.
- [`synap catalog`](#synap-catalog) — Validate, diff and publish the OFFICIAL template catalog (workspaces, capabilities, skills, packs, automations) from the monorepo checkout
  - [`synap catalog validate`](#synap-catalog-validate) — Validate the catalog (per-kind schema, cross-kind refs, goal grammar, duplicates) — offline
  - [`synap catalog diff`](#synap-catalog-diff) — Show what would change against the live control-plane catalog (new / changed / unchanged)
  - [`synap catalog publish`](#synap-catalog-publish) — Validate, preview the diff, confirm, then publish to the control plane — founder only: --official + a `synap login` session that owns synap-official
- [`synap capability`](#synap-capability) — The one capability-first root: list, add, enable, connect, show, run a capability pack
  - [`synap capability list`](#synap-capability-list) — List capabilities — one row per pack, with status, connection, and verbs
  - [`synap capability add`](#synap-capability-add) — Install a capability from the catalog — omit the name to pick from a list
  - [`synap capability create`](#synap-capability-create) — Create a capability from a JSON definition (file path, or pipe JSON via stdin)
  - [`synap capability rm`](#synap-capability-rm) — Remove capability container(s) by id or name — member tools/skills untouched
  - [`synap capability enable`](#synap-capability-enable) — Turn on a capability — omit the name to pick from a list; ensures its connection, then pick which verbs it can do
  - [`synap capability connect`](#synap-capability-connect) — Connect a service — omit the name to pick from connectable services
  - [`synap capability disconnect`](#synap-capability-disconnect) — Disconnect a capability's service — accepts a capability name or a provider id
  - [`synap capability show`](#synap-capability-show) — Show one capability's full detail: status, connection, verbs, next action
  - [`synap capability run`](#synap-capability-run) — Launch a verb — pass inputs as `--key value` flags
  - [`synap capability test`](#synap-capability-test) — Dry-run a verb (preview side effects without executing)
  - [`synap capability connections`](#synap-capability-connections) — Manage a capability's connections: list, add, update, rm
    - [`synap capability connections list`](#synap-capability-connections-list) — List a capability's connections (label, kind, default, context, id)
    - [`synap capability connections add`](#synap-capability-connections-add) — Add a connection — prompts for label + masked value unless provided as flags
    - [`synap capability connections update`](#synap-capability-connections-update) — Update a connection's fields; --rotate (or --value) rotates its secret
    - [`synap capability connections rm`](#synap-capability-connections-rm) — Remove a connection by id (confirms first)
  - [`synap capability sync-status`](#synap-capability-sync-status) — Show sync status per provider × kind × connection (phase, counts, errors) — omit provider to see all
- [`synap sync`](#synap-sync) — Sync status for connected providers — see `cap sync-status`
  - [`synap sync status`](#synap-sync-status) — Show sync status per provider × kind × connection (phase, counts, errors) — omit provider to see all. Alias of `synap cap sync-status`.
- [`synap providers`](#synap-providers) — LLM providers on the pod (OpenAI/Anthropic/…) for local coding tools — not capability packs
  - [`synap providers list`](#synap-providers-list) — Show enabled AI providers and their models
  - [`synap providers pull`](#synap-providers-pull) — Write pod LLM credentials into opencode or aider, or print the OpenAI-compatible {pod}/v1 endpoint
  - [`synap providers set-key`](#synap-providers-set-key) — Store your own API key override for a provider (BYOI)
  - [`synap providers list-keys`](#synap-providers-list-keys) — List user/workspace-level provider key overrides
- [`synap keys`](#synap-keys) — Manage pod API keys
  - [`synap keys rotate`](#synap-keys-rotate) — Rotate your CLI key to pick up the latest scope set

## `synap`

```
synap [options] [command]
```

Synap CLI — connect AI agents to your data pod

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `-V, --version` | output the version number |  |
| `--pod <name>` | Run this command against a saved pod profile (overrides the default pod for this invocation only) |  |

## `synap init`

```
synap init [options]
```

Full setup: connect to a Synap pod and install the skill

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--pod-url <url>` | Synap pod URL (skip pod choice prompt) |  |
| `--api-key <key>` | Hub Protocol API key (skip key generation) |  |
| `-y, --yes` | Accept the defaults, no prompts (connects the agents found on this machine) |  |
| `--agents <list>` | Agents to connect, comma-separated: claude-code,codex,cursor |  |
| `--json` | Print a JSON summary on stdout: {podUrl, connected, notApproved, failed, pairLink, exitCode} |  |

```text
Exit codes:
  0  at least one agent connected
  2  not a terminal, or a bad flag (pass --pod-url and --agents)
  3  no pod found, created or reachable
  4  cancelled
  5  could not get your key for the pod (pass --api-key)
  6  the pod is ready but no agent was connected
```

## `synap capture`

```
synap capture [options] [text]
```

Capture knowledge: smart `capture "<free text>"` (AI structures it). For canonical typed Knowledge, use `create entity --profile=knowledge --props='{"knowledgeForm":"insight|caution"}'`.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | no |  |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--type <type>` | Legacy compatibility typed mode (gotcha\|lesson\|decision\|reference); new automation should use knowledgeForm |  |
| `--claim <text>` | Typed mode: one-line assertion (required with --type) |  |
| `--title <text>` | Typed mode: short name, 80 characters or less (default: the claim's first sentence, never cut) |  |
| `--content <markdown>` | Typed mode: full Markdown explanation, stored as the linked Knowledge note |  |
| `--why <text>` | Reasoning or context |  |
| `--evidence <text>` | Supporting file path, URL, or code snippet |  |
| `--tags <csv>` | Comma-separated tags e.g. repo:synap-backend,layer:migrations |  |
| `--session` | Link captured knowledge to the active session |  |
| `--pod-wide` | GLOBAL lane: pod-wide cross-cutting runbook (→ knowledge_keys), visible in every workspace |  |
| `--global` | Alias for --pod-wide |  |
| `--key <ns:slug>` | Stable key for a --pod-wide runbook (derived from --type + --claim if omitted) |  |
| `--team` | Pin to the first product workspace (default: omit workspaceId — server-derived / pod-wide preferred for knowledge) |  |
| `--workspace <id>` | Explicit workspace pin (otherwise workspaceId is omitted for knowledge) |  |
| `--project <id\|name>` | Pin the capture to a project (id or name) — overrides SYNAP_PROJECT_ID / the session lens |  |
| `--yes` | Skip the y/N confirmation prompt (smart mode) |  |
| `--json` | Output as JSON |  |

## `synap import`

```

```

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `inputs` | no |  (variadic) |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--workspace <id\|name>` | Override AI workspace routing |  |
| `--project <id\|name>` | Override AI project routing |  |
| `--home-map <pairs>` | Multi-home path map: pathSubstring=workspaceNameOrId pairs (e.g. "Projects=Builder,Posts=Content OS"). Matched batch paths are rewritten with the workspace name as the first segment so placement heuristics pin the right home. No product defaults. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Preview only — do not write |  |
| `--yes` | Skip confirmation / auto-confirm store-first |  |
| `--session` | Link created entities to the active session |  |
| `--json` | Output as JSON |  |
| `--pod-url <url>` | Pod URL override |  |
| `--api-key <key>` | API key override |  |
| `--source <name>` | Adapter: superwhisper (paired meta.json+output.wav store-first) |  |
| `--store-first` | Skip AI structure; store units as pod-wide notes (+ optional audio) |  |
| `--keep-raw` | Keep the original file and link it to the created entity (default: extract, then discard the bytes) |  |
| `--with-audio` | Upload WAV provenance (default on for --source superwhisper --store-first) |  |
| `--no-with-audio` | Transcript-only (no WAV upload) |  |
| `--limit <n>` | Max Superwhisper units to process |  |
| `--concurrency <n>` | Parallel unit uploads (1–4) |  |
| `--no-resume` | Ignore local import ledger (re-import all) |  |
| `--job-status <jobId>` | Re-poll a background corpus import started by an earlier run (no waiting) |  |

| Option | Description | Default |

| `--json` | Output as JSON |  |
| `--pod-url <url>` | Pod URL override |  |
| `--api-key <key>` | API key override |  |

```text
Examples:
  synap upload ./report.pdf
  synap upload ./logo.png --title "Brand logo" --workspace <id>
  synap upload ./spec.pdf --attach <entityId>
  synap upload ./logo.svg --profile brand-asset --prop variant=dark --workspace <id>
  synap upload ./launch.mp4 --workspace <id>
  synap upload ./report.pdf --open
```

## `synap session wait`

```
synap session wait [options] [sessionId]
```

Block until the human replies in the session room (or, with --events, until the session changes), then print it. Session: the argument, else the one attached to this terminal. Exit 0 replied · 1 timeout · 2 failure (auth/network/broken read); with --hook: 2 wake · 0 anything else

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sessionId` | no |  |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--since <iso>` | Only events strictly after this ISO timestamp (default: now — skips anything that predates this wait; with --events: the unread ones) |  |
| `--events <kinds>` | Wait on the session change feed: comma list of answer, proposal_decided, stage_moved, owner_message, session_message (a message from another session's agent), or all |  |
| `--wake-only` | Stop only on what should wake an agent: answers, owner messages, and agent messages the pod marked wake (the rest is read and skipped) |  |
| `--once` | One read, no waiting loop |  |
| `--peek` | Mark nothing picked up or read (a watcher that is not the agent doing the work) |  |
| `--hook` | Run as a Claude Code asyncRewake Stop hook: wait for a wake-worthy event, print it on stderr, exit 2 (see: synap hooks install-wake) |  |
| `--timeout <duration>` | Give up after this long (e.g. 30m, 2h) | `"30m"` |
| `--interval <duration>` | Delay between checks of the answer-only wait (e.g. 10s) | `"10s"` |
| `--limit <n>` | Max answers / events per page, 1-100 | `"20"` |
| `--json` | Output the reply(ies) or events — or the timeout — as JSON |  |
| `--pod-url <url>` | Pod URL override |  |
| `--api-key <key>` | API key override |  |

## `synap session post`

```
synap session post [options] <toSessionId> <text...>
```

Message ANOTHER of your sessions' agent: blocked_on_you / handoff may wake it, done / fyi never do. Replying to a message that woke you? Pass its id as --cause. Exit 0 delivered · 1 pod does not deliver agent messages · 2 failure

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `toSessionId` | yes |  |
| `text` | yes |  (variadic) |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--intent <intent>` | blocked_on_you \| handoff \| done \| fyi | `"fyi"` |
| `--cause <messageId>` | The message that woke you (the id `synap session wait` printed), when this replies to it |  |
| `--from <sessionId>` | Your session, when this terminal is not bound to it |  |
| `--ref <kind:id[:label]>` | The state behind the message: session:<id>, blocked_by:<id>, proposal:<id>, slot:<sessionId>:<label> (repeatable) | `[]` |
| `--json` | Output the pod's reply as JSON |  |
| `--pod-url <url>` | Pod URL override |  |
| `--api-key <key>` | API key override |  |

## `synap track status`

```
synap track status [options] <id> <status>
```

Move a track: proposed|agreed|ready|active|paused|completed (Closed)|archived (Dropped). Closing needs --verdict met|partly_met|not_met (an operation closes retired, and only one does); dropping should carry no_longer_needed|impossible|replaced|mistake (impossible and replaced need --verdict-reason). Both are final — reopen makes a new version.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes |  |
| `status` | yes |  |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--verdict <verdict>` | How the goal ended (required to close; advised to drop) |  |
| `--verdict-reason <text>` | Why — required for impossible and replaced |  |
| `--expected <status>` | The status you read the goal in (synap track show) — refused, nothing written, if it moved meanwhile. Agents: always pass it |  |
| `--reason <text>` | Why — shown to the reviewer |  |
| `--json` | Output as JSON |  |
| `--pod-url <url>` | Pod URL override |  |
| `--api-key <key>` | API key override |  |

## `synap cell`

```
synap cell [options] [command]
```

Define and bundle frame cells for the Synap runtime

Subcommands: [`define`](#synap-cell-define), [`build`](#synap-cell-build)

## `synap cell define`

```
synap cell define [options]
```

Create or update a frame cell on the pod from ESM source

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--name <name>` | Cell display name (required) |  |
| `--file <path>` | ESM source file (or pipe stdin) |  |
| `--type-key <key>` | Explicit typeKey (default: generated:<slug>) |  |
| `--deps <json>` | Dependency map JSON, e.g. '{"recharts":"2.12.0"}' |  |
| `--view-types <list>` | Comma-separated view types this cell can render as a VIEW RENDERER, e.g. "list,table,kanban". Omit to leave an existing affinity untouched; pass "" to clear it |  |
| `--content-kind <kind>` | What this cell renders — entity-detail \| entity-card \| entity-profile \| collection \| widget (default: widget, which is placeable but never offered as a profile renderer) |  |
| `--workspace <id>` | Workspace to scope the cell to (default: your active workspace lens — run `synap lens` to see it) |  |
| `--description <text>` | Short description |  |
| `--open` | Open in the Synap desktop app after define |  |
| `--json` | JSON output |  |
| `--pod-url <url>` | Pod URL override |  |
| `--api-key <key>` | API key override |  |

```text
Without --view-types / --content-kind a cell installs cleanly but can never be
PICKED as a view or profile renderer — it is only placeable on a bento.

Examples:
  synap cell define --name "Revenue Chart" --file ./chart.js
  synap cell define --name "Revenue Chart" --file ./chart.js --deps '{"recharts":"2.12.0"}'
  synap cell define --name "Deal Board" --file ./board.js --view-types kanban,table --content-kind collection
  synap cell define --name "Contact Page" --file ./contact.js --content-kind entity-detail
  cat chart.js | synap cell define --name "Revenue Chart"
```

## `synap cell build`

```
synap cell build [options] <entry>
```

Bundle a multi-file cell/app into a single ESM module the runtime expects

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `entry` | yes |  |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--out <file>` | Output file path (default: <entry>.bundle.js) |  |
| `--bundle-deps` | Inline all third-party deps into the bundle (only react/react-dom stay external) — output has deps={} and the runtime CSP drops esm.sh entirely |  |
| `--self-contained` | Build ONE complete HTML document (React, CSS, brand fonts inlined; nothing external) — the code of a rendererType "mcp-app" cell |  |
| `--fonts` | With --self-contained: require the inlined brand fonts (default: include when @synap-core/design-tokens resolves) |  |
| `--no-fonts` | With --self-contained: skip the inlined brand fonts |  |
| `--define` | Chain into cell define after bundling (requires --name) |  |
| `--name <name>` | Cell name (required with --define) |  |
| `--type-key <key>` | Explicit typeKey (used with --define) |  |
| `--deps <json>` | Override dependency versions as JSON, e.g. '{"react":"18.3.0"}' |  |
| `--view-types <list>` | Comma-separated view-renderer affinity (used with --define), e.g. "list,table" |  |
| `--content-kind <kind>` | entity-detail \| entity-card \| entity-profile \| collection \| widget (used with --define) |  |
| `--workspace <id>` | Workspace (used with --define) |  |
| `--description <text>` | Description (used with --define) |  |
| `--open` | Open in browser after define (used with --define) |  |
| `--json` | JSON output |  |
| `--pod-url <url>` | Pod URL override |  |
| `--api-key <key>` | API key override |  |

```text
Output: a single ESM file.

Default mode: bare imports (react, recharts, …) are externalized and emitted
as a deps map. At runtime Synap resolves them via esm.sh importmap.

--bundle-deps mode: only react/react-dom are externalized (React is
host-inlined at runtime, never via esm.sh); everything else is bundled into
the output, so the deps map is empty. A cell built this way reaches no esm.sh
origin at runtime — the runtime CSP collapses to drop it entirely.

Examples:
  synap cell build ./src/chart.tsx --out ./dist/chart.js
  synap cell build ./src/chart.tsx --out ./dist/chart.js --define --name "Revenue Chart"
  synap cell build ./src/chart.tsx --out ./dist/chart.js --bundle-deps
```

## `synap market publish`

```
synap market publish [options] [targets...]
```

Validate then publish a template (or a standalone cell/view package) to the marketplace (private by default) — pass a file, --from-workspace <id>, or --from-project <id>. Non-official publish never uses the synap-official vendor. Founder: --official [slug...] publishes the official catalog from the monorepo checkout (alias of `synap catalog publish --official --kind workspace`)

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `targets` | no |  (variadic) |

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--official` | Publish the OFFICIAL Synap catalog (all templates, or the named slugs) from the monorepo checkout — requires a `synap login` session that owns the synap-official vendor; previews and asks first |  |
| `--templates-dir <dir>` | With --official: path to the catalog package — synap-app/packages/catalog or workspace-templates (default: found by walking up from cwd) |  |
| `--dry-run` | With --official: preview what would change against the live catalog, publish nothing |  |
| `--yes` | With --official: skip the confirmation prompt |  |
| `--public` | Publish as PUBLIC (default is private) |  |
| `--private` | Publish as private (the default — stated explicitly) |  |
| `--from-workspace <id>` | Serialize a live workspace into a template and publish it (instead of a file) |  |
| `--from-project <id>` | Serialize a live project's used workspaces into a suite package (tags: suite, require deps) and publish it |  |
| `--price <usd>` | Stamp pricingModel=one_time + priceUsd (dollars→cents). Settlement/Stripe is not this wave — columns only. |  |
| `--json` | Output as JSON |  |
| `--pod-url <url>` | Pod URL override (for --from-workspace / --from-project) |  |
| `--api-key <key>` | API key override (for --from-workspace / --from-project) |  |
| `--no-bundle-deps` | Publish a cell's codeFile with external deps via esm.sh instead of bundling them in (default: bundled) |  |

| `--api-key <key>` | API key override |  |
